title: LLAMP: Assessing Network Latency Tolerance of HPC Applications with Linear Programming
problem: Network latency in HPC clusters has increased due to high-bandwidth architectures designed for AI workloads, adversely affecting communication-intensive applications. Current methods to assess network latency tolerance rely on specialized hardware or time-consuming simulators.
motivation: Understanding network latency tolerance is critical for optimizing HPC application performance as data centers shift toward high-bandwidth network architectures.
method: LLAMP combines the LogGPS model with linear programming to analytically predict HPC applications' network latency tolerance without specialized hardware or simulation. The toolchain instruments MPI applications to extract communication patterns and parameters. Linear programming determines the maximum acceptable network latency threshold before performance degradation occurs. Validation on LULESH, MILC, and ICON demonstrates prediction errors below 2%.
key_novelty: Uses linear programming over the LogGPS model to analytically predict network latency tolerance of HPC applications without requiring specialized hardware or simulation.
contributions: LLAMP toolchain combining LogGPS model with linear programming for analytical network latency tolerance assessment
Demonstrates high prediction accuracy (< 2% error) on diverse MPI applications including LULESH and MILC
Applicability to collective algorithms and network topologies demonstrated through ICON weather and climate model case study
primary_theme: Network latency tolerance analysis for HPC
